Pesticides and Pesticides Residue Analysis Sectional Committee, FAD 1

FOREWORD This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Pesticides and Pesticides Residue Analysis Sectional Committee had-been approved by the Food and Agriculture Division Council. Chlorimuron ethyl, technical is employed in the preparation of herbicidal formulations for agricultural use.

Chlorimuron ethyl is the accepted common name by the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) for ethyl 2-{ [[[(4 -Chloro-6-methoxypyrimidin-2- yl)amino]-carbony l]amino]sulfony l}benzoate. The empirical and structural formuke and the molecular mass of chlorimuron ethyl are given below:
Empirical Formula Structural Formula Molecular Mass

o
In preparation of this standard, due consideration has been given to the provisions of the Insecticides Act, 1968 and the Rules framed thereunder. However, this standard is subject to the restrictions imposed under the Insecticides Act and Rules, wherever applicable. For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2:1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)'. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

ANNEX A [(Tab/e 1, Item (i)]
DETERMINATION A-1 PRINCIPLE OF CHLORIMURON ETHYL CONTENT

A-3 REAGENTS A-3. 1 Acetonitrile,

Chlorimuron ethyl content is determined by high performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) using internal standard technique. A-2 APPARATUS A-2. 1 A high performance liquid chromatography system coupled with ultraviolet detector and a printer -- plotter-cum-integrator is used for this determination. The suggested operative parameters are as follows, but can be changed if necessary, provided standardization is done. Column : ODS, 250 mm x 4.6 mm, with a 0.5 ~m in-line filter (Filter required to protect the analytical column) : Ambient : Acetonitrile: Water (43:57, v/v),pH of water =3.0 adjusted with 85 percent phosphoric acid (HJPOd) : 2.0 ml/min : Ultraviolet detector (234 nm)
Balance

HPLC grade.

A-3.2 Water, HPLC grade. A-3.3 Phosphoric
Acid, HPLC grade, 85.0 percent.

A-3.4 Ammonium Hydroxide, 0.024 N. A-3.5 Phenyl Sulfone (Internal Standard), of known purity.
A-3.6 Chlorimuron Ethyl Analytical Standard,

of

known purity. A-4 `PROCEDURE A-4.1 Preparation
of Internal Standard

Temperature Mobile phase

Weigfi 360 mg of phenyl sulfone into a 1000 ml volumetric flask and dissolve ultrasonically in 400 ml of acetonitrile. Cool the solution to room temperature and make up to volume with O.024N NHiOH and shake to mix. A-4.2 Preparation
of Standard Solution

Flow rate Detector
A-2.2 Analytical

Injection volume : 20 microlitre

A-2.3 pH Meter A-2.4 A-2.5 A-2.6 A-2.7 Microlitre Syringe, 25 microlitre.

Weigh accurately 50 mg of chlorimuron ethyl analytical standard into a 50 ml volumetric flask. Pipette 20.0 ml of acetonitrile into the flask and ultrasonicate for 10 min to dissolve. Equilibrate the solution to room temperature and dilute to volume with 0.024 N NHiOH. Label the flask as `Standard stock solution'. Pipette 10.0 ml of internal standard solution into a 25 ml volumetric flask. Add 5.0 ml of the standard stock solution into the 25 ml volumetric flask. Make up to volume, if necessary, with 40/60 mixture of acetonitrile/O.024 N NHiOH and shake to mix well. Label flask as `Standard working solution'. 2

Filter Units, 0.5 pm and 0.45 ~m. Ultrasonic Standard Bath Glassware

IS 15619:2005 A-4.3 Preparation of Sample Solution

Weigh accurately 100 mg of chlorimuron ethyl, technical in a 100 ml volumetric flask. Add 40 ml acetonitrile and ultrasonicate for 10 min. Equilibrate to room temperature for 15 min and then make up to volume with 0.024 N NHOOH. Pipette 5.0 ml of this solution in a 25 ml volumetric flask and add 10.0 ml of the internal standard solution into the flask. Make up to volume, if necessary, with 40/60 mixture of acetonitrile/O.024 N NHiOH and shake to mix well.
A-4.4 A-4.4.1 Estimation

of the active ingredient and the internal standard and calculate the percentage of the active ingredient as given in A-5. A-5 CALCULATION Chlorimuron ethyl content,
percent m~m = M1x A~x A2x P Mz x A4 x A,

where M, = mass of chlorimuron ethyl in standard solution, in g; M, = mass of the sample taken for test, in g; A, = peak area of chlorimuron ethyl in the chromatogram of standard solution; A, = peak area of chlorimuron ethyl in the chromatogram of sample solution; A, = peak area of internal standard, phenyl sulfone, in the chromatogram of standard solution; A, = peak area of internal standard, phenyl sulfone, in the chromatogram of sample solution; and P= percentage purity of chlorimuron ethyl in reference standard.

Filter a portion of all sample and standard solutions through a 0.45 ~m filter unit before analysis. After the column has been equilibrated and a stable baseline is obtained, inject, in duplicate, 20 microlitre each of standard and sample solution. BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 to promote harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and attending to connected matters in the country. Copyright BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director (Publications), BIS. `Review of Indian Standards Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of `BIS Catalogue' and `Standards : Monthly Additions'.
